SignedOut.title: Signed out
SignedOut.notAdminExplanation: This account can't administer Kale (it doesn't hold auth.Admin); it has been signed out.
SignedOut.sessionEndedExplanation: It was stopped by an administrator, it expired or couldn't be renewed, or you signed in somewhere else. Sign in again to continue.

NotAdmin.title: Not allowed
NotAdmin.explanation: This account can't administer Kale (it doesn't hold auth.Admin).

Forms.invalid: AuthService refused the change; check the values.
Forms.notFound: It no longer exists (perhaps removed in another tab). Reload the page.
Forms.secretShownOnce: Copy it now: it is shown only this once (AuthService keeps only its hash). Store it as the application's Podman secret.

Applications.title: Applications
Applications.explanation: The applications that sign their users in with Kale. Each registers its own operations; roles grant them.
Applications.newExplanation: Kale makes its client secret and shows it once.
Applications.keyHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. Can't be changed later.
Applications.name: Name
Applications.onePerLine: One address per line; https (http only for localhost). Leave empty for an API without a web front end.
Applications.confirmRotate: Replace the client secret of {key}? The current one stops working at once.
Applications.confirmDeactivate: Deactivate {key}? Nobody can sign in to it, and its open sessions stop being accepted.
Applications.adminUiSecret: The admin UI's own secret: replace it with the admin UI's Podman secret, not here.

Application.name: Name
Application.onePerLine: One address per line; https (http only for localhost, in local development).
Application.keyIsPermanent: The key can't change: it is the application's client id, its tokens' audience and its operations' prefix.
Application.adminUiAddresses: This is the admin UI itself: its return addresses are set when Kale is set up (admin bootstrap) and can't be changed.
Application.secretExplanation: The application uses it to sign users in and to call Kale. Kale keeps only its hash.
Application.activeExplanation: Users with access can sign in.
Application.inactiveExplanation: Nobody can sign in, and its sessions aren't accepted.

Error.title: Something went wrong
Error.explanation: The page couldn't be loaded or the change couldn't be made. AuthService may be unreachable.

Roles.title: Roles
Roles.explanation: A role grants operations of this application. Users get roles directly or through groups.
Roles.name: Name
Roles.operationsExplanation: The application registers these itself at startup; they can't be added here.
Roles.obsolete: Obsolete: no longer registered by the application
Roles.noOperations: The application hasn't registered any operations yet (it does at startup).

Role.operationsExplanation: Everyone with this role can do these (and what they imply). Changes apply at once, also to users signed in now.
Role.obsolete: Obsolete: no longer registered; dropped at the next change
Role.noOperations: This role grants no operations yet.
Role.confirmRemove: Remove {operation} from {name}? Everyone with this role loses it at once.
Role.addExplanation: Everyone with this role gains them at once.
Role.nothingToAdd: The role already holds every current operation.
Role.obsoleteDropped: The role also holds obsolete operations; they are dropped with this change: {operations}
Role.name: Name
Role.confirmDelete: Delete the role {name}? Its open sessions stop at once, and users and groups lose it.

Users.title: Users
Users.explanation: Accounts that sign in with Kale. A user needs access to an application and a role in it.
Users.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. Give it to the user through a safe channel.

User.disabledExplanation: can't sign in; their sessions were stopped
User.confirmDisable: Disable {userName}? All their sessions stop at once and they can't sign in.
User.applicationsHint: Signing in to an application needs active access to it and a role (direct or through a group).
User.noApplications: No access to any application yet.
User.confirmAccess: Save the access to {key}? Making it inactive stops their sessions there at once.
User.rolesHint: Roles from groups are on the groups.
User.assignExplanation: The user holds them at once; signing in to an application also needs access to it.
User.noRolesLeft: The user already holds every role directly.
User.confirmUnassign: Remove the role {role} ({key})? Their sessions with it stop, unless a group still grants it.
User.groupsHint: The user holds every role of these groups.

Groups.title: Groups
Groups.explanation: Members of a group hold all of its roles (groups don't nest).
Groups.name: Name

Group.name: Name
Group.confirmDelete: Delete the group {name}? Its members lose its roles, and their sessions with those roles stop (unless they still hold them another way).
Group.confirmRemoveMember: Remove {userName} from the group? Their sessions with the group's roles stop (unless they still hold them another way).
Group.addMembersExplanation: They hold the group's roles at once.
Group.noUsersLeft: Every user is already a member.
Group.rolesHint: Every member holds these roles. Signing in also needs active access to the application (on the user's page).
Group.confirmRemoveRole: Remove the role {role} ({key}) from the group? Members' sessions with it stop (unless they still hold it another way).
Group.addRolesExplanation: Every member holds them at once.
Group.noRolesLeft: The group already holds every role.

Sessions.title: Open sessions
Sessions.explanation: Signed in and not yet ended or expired. Times are in {timeZone}.
Sessions.confirmStop: Stop this session of {userName} in {key}? The application refuses it at once; they have to sign in again.

TestToken.title: Test token
TestToken.explanation: A user's access token to an application, to try your API before it has a sign-in page. Kale refuses this outside development.
TestToken.sideEffect: It's a real sign-in of that user (under the normal rules: active user, access and role), so it ends their other session in that application.
TestToken.roleHint: A role of the chosen application.
TestToken.tokenNote: Shown only here; get a new one when it expires.
TestToken.try: Call your API with it, for example:
